sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the United States of America (entry into force 14 May 1991)
Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Panama and the United States of America (entry into force 31 October 2012)
Double Taxation Agreement between the Republic of Panama and the Kingdom of the Netherlands (entry into force 2011)
Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the Republic of Singapore (signed 2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015, as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019 and Ley No. 129 de 2020 (AML/CFT framework), together with the implementing regulations of the Superintendencia de Bancos and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero, and the Reglamento del Beneficiario Final issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI). Private Interest Foundations are governed by Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995. Resident agents are subject to the Consolidated AML Manual applicable to non-financial parties.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the founder's certificate of incorporation, by-laws, and certificate of good standing (where the founder is a corporate entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or Ministry of Justice of the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization at the Consulate of Panama in the jurisdiction of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Founding Deed and Foundation Charter executed before a Panamanian notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public / licensed resident agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama; no apostille required if executed in Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Declaration of Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s) and PEP status declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Resident agent / Dirección General de Ingresos (Registro de Beneficiario Final)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private filing with the resident agent and DGI; not subject to consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of account or independent auditor for the founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or certified bank stamp witnessed and authenticated by the resident agent

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory four-list screening of all founders, foundation council members, beneficiaries, and UBOs against (i) OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP), and (iv) the national terrorist watch-list maintained by the Panamanian Unidad de Análisis Financiero. Two-step identity verification (identification plus confirmation of identity) is required under Ley 23/2015. Beneficiaries of charitable grants must be re-screened immediately prior to each distribution and upon any material change to the grant schedule.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Official Online Name Reservation and Clearance Service (Servicio en Línea del Registro Público)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All official record entries are in Spanish. A company or foundation name may be in any language using the Latin alphabet but must be transliterated into Spanish-readable phonetics and accompanied by a Spanish translation for registry indexing. Names of private interest foundations must contain the denomination 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Foundation' when expressed in English. The name must not contravene public order or bona fide customs.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 5 business days of a name rejection, the applicant (acting through the resident agent) may file a 'recurso de reconsideración' with the Dirección General del Registro Público, attaching a certified name-search report and the official fee receipt (approx. USD 15–25). If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an 'recurso de apelación' before the Superior Court within 20 business days. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately re-submit the same name with a substantially modified phrase structure or a different distinctive token. A fee waiver is granted for re-submission made within the original 30-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a private charitable foundation and holding-type entities. The registered office may correspond to the licensed resident agent's physical Panamanian address. A physical office is not required for the foundation's day-to-day philanthropy, endowment management, or grant-distribution activities. However, regulated financial activities (banking, securities, fiduciary services, insurance) impose a physical-presence requirement and on-site management expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated 5% annual probability for a chartered private-interest foundation with no regulated financial activity. Probability increases to approximately 10–12% if the foundation engages in multi-jurisdiction cross-border wire transfers, or if a suspicious-activity report is filed by a correspondent bank.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and reservation fee (Registro Público de Panamá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Registry's official fee schedule (Tarifa del Registro Público)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarization of the constitution deed and foundation regulations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian Notary Public / external law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for formation of a private interest foundation; range USD 550–1,200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration inscription fee in the Register of Private Interest Foundations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee under Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial resident agent fee for the first year (registered office and official address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; statutory requirement under Panama corporate law

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register declaration and PEP/sanctions screening report preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional fee for mandatory KYC/AML file preparation under Ley No. 23 de 2015

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Fiscal registration with DGII (RUC) and municipal business-license presentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional fee for electronic submission and representation; RUC registration itself is non-fiscal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization services for founder's corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the founder's jurisdiction / legalization courier service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed consular and registration fees plus handling fee charged by the resident agent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley No. 41 de 24 de agosto de 2007; applicable Arts. 4-6 (constitution, initial patrimony, legal personality), 8-10 (contents and registration of the foundation deed), 14-20 (Foundation Council, Protector, Fiscal); supplemented by Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 for corporate governance analogies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section), Via España, Ciudad de Panamá, with digital filing through the e-Registry portal where available.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Carta Fundacional (Private Interest Foundation Deed, also known as Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado), executed as a notarized public instrument before a Panamanian Notario Público and inscribed in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The founding deed must assign an initial patrimony (endowment) adequate to achieve the foundation's object; market standard is USD 10,000. No escrow or deposit account is required for formation; the endowment may be in-kind or booked later, and a flat annual tax of USD 300 applies to foundations with no commercial activity under Ley 41 de 2007.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Founder acknowledges receipt of the subscribed initial endowment of US$10,000, irrevocably allocated as the Foundation's patrimony and dedicated exclusively to philanthropic, scientific and educational grant purposes. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office is fixed at Albrook, Corregimiento de Ancón, Distrito de Panamá, República de Panamá, and the Foundation Protector, Fiscal, and Secretary are duly appointed to administer the Foundation in accordance with Law 25 of 1995, as amended by Law 41 of 2007. RESOLVED FINALLY: The Foundation Council approves the internal Bylaws, authorizes opening of a corporate bank account with an SBP-licensed bank, and empowers the officers to execute grant distribution procedures, annual regulatory filings, and municipal licensing formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Foundation Name and Execute the Foundation Deed before a Panamanian Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Oficina de Nombres y Consultas; Notaría Pública of the Circuit of Panamá designated by the founding attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney (abogado idóneo). Submit a name-availability request to the Registro Público with three alternative foundation names. Draft the Carta Fundacional in Spanish containing the founder's identity, charitable object, initial endowment (patrimonio inicial), apportionment of assets to philanthropic and scientific grant purposes, and designation of the Foundation Council, Protector, and Fiscal. Execute the deed before a Notario Público, who protocolizes the instrument; obtain certified copies for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Name-availability request with three alternative foundation names
Identity documents of the natural or corporate founder
Draft of the Carta Fundacional covering object, endowment, apportionment, council, and beneficiaries
Evidence and source documentation of the initial patrimony (bank or in-kind assets)
Power of attorney if the founder is represented
Attorney's attestation of compliance with Ley 25 de 1995, as amended
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the proposed name, the attorney resubmits an alternative name with only a nominal re-filing token. If the notary issues a corrective note, the deed is re-executed as an enmendada corrective instrument and re-protocolized, extending completion by up to five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Foundation Deed in the Private Interest Foundations Section of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (physical counter or authorized electronic filing portal).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the notarized original Carta Fundacional and three certified copies at the Registry, pay the inscription fee at the official caja, and obtain the receipt. Upon assignment of the folio and issuance of the razon de inscripcion, the Foundation acquires separate legal personality. Retrieve the certified testimonio of the registered deed for all downstream licensing and banking steps.
required_dossiers: Notarized original of the Carta Fundacional
Three certified copies of the foundation deed
Registry cover sheet (formulario de inscripcion) with indexing data
Proof of payment of registry inscription fees
Settlement of fiscal stamps applicable at registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a razon or advertencia, the attorney cures the defects by filing a supplementary corrective deed within 30 days, preserving the original priority date; a surcharge per the Registry fee tariff applies only if resubmission exceeds the statutory grace period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain R.U.C. Tax Registration and the Municipal Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía de Panamá — Dirección General de Rentas Municipales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the registered testimonio and the Council resolution appointing fiscal representatives, apply for the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (R.U.C.) and obtain the NIT certificate. File the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality and pay the municipal licensing fee. If the Foundation conducts no commercial activity, file the first annual flat tax declaration of USD 300 under Ley 41 de 2007 and retain the payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Certified copy (testimonio) of the registered foundation deed
Certified copy of the Foundation Council resolution appointing officers
R.U.C. application form with signature certification
Lease contract or title proving the registered office address
Municipal Aviso de Operación form and fee payment
DGI annual flat tax declaration form with USD 300 payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI rejects the R.U.C. application due to deed-address discrepancies, file a corrective enmienda with the Registry or obtain a municipal certifiado de domicilio and re-present the application electronically within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Fire-Safety, Structural/Occupancy, and Occupational Clearances for the Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá — Dirección de Prevención y Seguridad; Municipio de Panamá — Dirección de Obras; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) — Dirección de Higiene y Seguridad Ocupacional.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the office floor plan and fire-safety application to the Bomberos, complete the on-site inspection, and obtain the Visto Bueno de Bomberos. Request the municipal Certificado de Uso/Ocupación evidencing structural-load conformity and permitted administrative use. If staff are engaged, register the employer with the Caja de Seguro Social and file the workplace health and safety program with MITRADEL for occupational clearance.
required_dossiers: Fire-safety application form and premises floor plan
Proof of installed extinguishers, emergency exit signage, and emergency lighting
Building lease or title and structural conformity certificate
Municipal Certificado de Uso application
Occupational health and safety program and CSS employer registration forms, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Bomberos inspection identifies deficiencies, install the required fire-suppression and emergency-lighting measures, request re-inspection within 10 business days, and pay the re-inspection fee. If the Municipality denies the Certificado de Uso on zoning grounds, relocate the registered office to a permitted commercial zone or obtain a special-use variance before re-applying.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the Foundation Bank Account and Execute Know-Your-Client and Grant-Distribution Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A banking institution licensed by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) and subject to AML supervision by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the registered foundation deed, the Council resolution authorizing the account, the R.U.C./NIT, and the Aviso de Operación to the chosen bank. Complete the bank's CDD/KYC forms identifying settlors, council members, and ultimate beneficiaries. Adopt a grant-distribution operating procedure with dual-signature authority and auditable record-keeping, and file the beneficial-ownership declaration where bank policy or UAF regulations require it.
required_dossiers: Registered Carta Fundacional and certified Council resolution for banking
R.U.C./NIT certificate and Aviso de Operación
Passports or national IDs of Protector, Fiscal, and authorized signatories
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds questionnaire
Signed AML/KYC compliance statement and grant-distribution policy
Municipal and fire clearances evidencing physical presence of the office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, supply the certified corporate genealogy and notarized source-of-wealth letters. If the account opening is declined, submit the dossier to a second SBP-licensed bank within 15 days, as each institution conducts an independent KYC assessment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá — Dirección General de Rentas Municipales (Municipal Licensing and Commercial Operations Desk); no industrial manufacturing board applies to ISIC 6430 office-based endowment and grant administration activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Operating Notice) supplemented by the Certificado de Personería Jurídica, the DGI R.U.C., and, for the physical premises, the Visto Bueno de Bomberos and Certificado de Uso (occupancy certificate).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III (Registro — low-impact administrative office use); no full Environmental Impact Study (EsIA) is required for ISIC 6430 office-based grant administration. If the Foundation later installs vaults, warehousing, or heavy electrical infrastructure, reclassification to Category II (Informe Ambiental) may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge sources are installed. Office wastewater must connect to the public IDAAN sewer network and comply with municipal pH 6-9 and BOD below 250 mg/L limits; no VOC or stack-emission thresholds apply to office-only operations. Solid waste must be segregated for AAUD municipal collection, and e-waste or spent UPS batteries must be delivered to MiAMBIENTE-licensed recyclers under the national residuals regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá must issue the Visto Bueno (fire-safety certificate) after inspection covering extinguishers, emergency exits, and emergency lighting. The Municipality issues the Certificado de Uso evidencing structural-load conformity and permitted office occupancy. MITRADEL's Dirección de Higiene y Seguridad Ocupacional performs an occupational hygiene inspection and accepts the workplace health and safety program; all employees must be registered with the Caja de Seguro Social.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; unitary national tax administration with no sub-national income tax or VAT authorities. Electronic services are centralized in the DGI e-Tax portal (Sistema T@x, integrated with SIGMEF) and the DGI Electronic Invoicing platform (Facturación Electrónica); customs matters are administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) in coordination with DGI for export substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the S.A. before a Panamanian notary and register the public deed with the Registro Público de Panamá; appoint a licensed resident agent (agente residente) and maintain a registered office in Panama. No minimum paid-in capital is required. Step 2: File the Aviso de Operación with the DGI (business-license aviso integrated under Law 254 of 2019) to obtain the fiscal identity (Registro Único de Contribuyente, RUC), which for juridical persons corresponds to the corporate cédula jurídica assigned at incorporation. Step 3: Submit the DGI taxpayer registration form through the DGI portal or through the resident agent, declaring the fiscal domicile, statutory officers, and the ISIC 6430 activity; obtain the RUC registration certificate and register for ITBMS if any taxable commercial supply will be carried out. Step 4: Obtain the FEA digital signature certificate (Firma Electrónica Avanzada) enabling e-filing, electronic invoicing, and Customs SDA system access. Step 5 (charitable election): file with DGI the constitutive documents and internal regulations demonstrating the non-profit, philanthropic or scientific purpose and the non-distribution constraint, and apply for the resolucion de calificacion as entidad sin fines de lucro (tax-exempt qualification). Equivalent RUC/aviso registration applies where the vehicle is structured as a Fundacion de Interes Privado under Law 25 of 1995. Foreign entities operating through a Panamanian branch additionally register the sucursal under the parent RUC after inscribing the branch deed in the Registro Publico. The RUC is kept in good standing by payment of the flat annual franchise tax (tasa única) and by filing annual informational returns even when no tax is due.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not recognize check-the-box or partnership pass-through elections; an S.A. is a per se entity-level taxpayer (25% ISR on Panamanian-source income only). Under territoriality, foreign-source endowment income, foreign capital gains, and offshore grants are automatically outside the tax base and require no election. Available statutory elections and regimes: (i) DGI non-profit qualification under Article 6(f) of the Codigo Fiscal, conferring ISR exemption on institutional income (donations, grants, endowment earnings) for charitable, educational, scientific, or social-assistance entities whose statutes prohibit profit distribution; (ii) reorganization into or registration as a Fundacion de Interes Privado under Law 25 of 1995 with fixed annual taxation and confidentiality rules, subject to RUC/DGI registration; (iii) ITBMS simplified small-taxpayer regime (Regimen Simplificado de Tributacion) for annual gross receipts up to USD 36,000; (iv) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying regional control or service functions, not applicable to a pure charitable endowment; (v) free-zone customs/ITBMS regimes in the Colón Free Zone, Panama Pacifico, and similar areas. Hybrid-mismatch and fiscal-transparency elections are not available under Panamanian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT-equivalent governed by the Codigo Fiscal (Articles 1057 et seq.) as amended by Law 254 of 2019; territorial scope limited to supplies of movable goods and services consumed in Panama.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Standard ITBMS registration is required for all legal entities from the commencement of taxable commercial activity in Panama, with no statutory de minimis turnover threshold for corporations. An optional simplified small-taxpayer (pequeno contribuyente) regime applies where annual gross receipts do not exceed USD 36,000. A charitable S.A. or foundation performing only exempt grant-making and endowment management, with no taxable supplies, must obtain from the DGI an ITBMS exclusion certificate (certificado de exclusion) to avoid mandatory registration; donations and grants are outside the scope of ITBMS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electronica) applies to all taxpayers under Law 254 of 2019 and DGI technical resolutions. Invoices must be generated through the DGI electronic-invoicing platform or certified private software connected to DGI web-service APIs; each invoice is transmitted to the DGI and validated online before or at issuance, receiving a unique fiscal folio, authentication code (código de seguridad), and QR code (prior-validation model). Export invoices, credit/debit notes, and purchase receipts must use the same digital channel, and access requires the taxpayer's FEA digital certificate. There is no physical fiscal stamping; the DGI online validation operates as fiscal clearance, and ITBMS returns are filed electronically on a monthly basis through the T@x portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated (0% ITBMS) where the goods physically depart Panamanian customs territory and title passes to a non-resident, evidenced by the customs export declaration and transport documents. Cross-border services qualify for zero-rating when performed for a non-resident recipient, wholly used abroad, and not connected with Panamanian real property; offshore asset-management, advisory, and grant-coordination services for foreign charitable donors fall within this category, while bare endowment holding and grant distributions are outside ITBMS scope for lack of a taxable supply. The exporter must issue an electronic invoice reflecting 0% ITBMS and retain the full documentary trail; input ITBMS on export-related purchases is creditable and recoverable through monthly offset or export refund (devolucion) under DGI rules using supplier export-certificates. Panama levies no VAT on exports and maintains no exchange-control repatriation requirement (the U.S. dollar is legal tender); the 180-day benchmark reflects interbank and DGI audit expectations for documentary collection closure and evidenced receipt of proceeds from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / Documento Único de Aduana, DUA) filed via the Customs SDA system
Signed Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de Embarque) or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from Panamanian territory
DGI electronic export invoice at 0% ITBMS bearing the fiscal validation code and QR
Export sales contract or service agreement with the foreign recipient
Inward remittance certificate (comprobante de transferencia bancaria / certificado de ingreso de divisas) evidencing collection from abroad
Packing list and certificate of origin, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ITBMS export claims are subject to ex-post documentary audit by DGI and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas. Where the goods are not exported or the service is not consumed abroad within the required period, the supply is recharacterized as domestic, triggering retroactive assessment of 7% ITBMS, statutory moratory interest, surcharges, and fines computed on the tax at issue. False or simulated export documentation constitutes tax fraud under the Codigo Fiscal: consequences include administrative fines, suspension or revocation of the RUC, closure of the establishment for up to 20 working days under Law 254 of 2019, loss of the non-profit qualification with retroactive recapture of exempt income, and, for willful evasion, criminal liability with imprisonment. The charitable S.A. or foundation must therefore retain export and foreign-income documentation for the statutory prescription period (generally five years) and, for grantees, must evidence non-profit use of funds to preserve the DGI qualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in Panama; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) governs bank licensing and AML/CFT compliance, while the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) administers external financial policy and public debt; the U.S. dollar serves as official legal tender with Federal Reserve monetary anchor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy with unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account; there are no currency controls, no dual exchange rates, and no impediments to profit remittance or philanthropic grant distribution; territorial taxation further shields offshore-source charitable endowments from local income tax, and cross-border contributions may be received and disbursed freely in USD or any mutually agreed foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no mandatory timeline, no surrender threshold, and no conversion ratio for export receipts; exporters and licensed private interest foundations may retain all proceeds in USD or exchange them at market rates through SBP-regulated commercial banks.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Foreign digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) do not possess Panamanian banking licenses and cannot independently maintain demand deposit accounts; they may provide payment initiation or card-clearing services only through a licensed local commercial bank in a correspondent-facilitator model. Acceptance by Panamanian banks is discretionary and depends on the applicant's source of funds documentation and the bank's correspondent banking appetite for non-resident private charitable foundations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panamanian law and SBP Rule 2-2013 do not categorically mandate physical appearance of directors or officers; banks may accept remote onboarding using authenticated video interviews, digital identity verification, and notarized/apostilled corporate records for registered low-risk .D/D classification. Nevertheless, private charitable foundations involved in cross-border grant flows should expect at least one video substantive interview, additional beneficial-owner attestations, and periodic physical or virtual follow-up if the bank adopts a enhanced due diligence stance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth and source of funds for the initial endowment or donation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete donor declaration, bank reference letters, audited financial statements or tax returns for the donor, notarized gift/endowment resolution, and a detailed explanation of the transaction rationale consistent with the foundation's charitable purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation has no tangible business substance or physical presence in Panama; nominee officers or protectors are used
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide foundation charter with apostille, current board resolutions, registered agent appointment, sworn statement of non-nominal activity, evidence of retention of local legal counsel/accounting office, and a business/substance narrative showing grant selection and monitoring functions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) involved as settlor, protector, or beneficiary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit PEP declarations from all relevant parties, independent source-of-funds verification, enhanced due diligence questionnaires, media/negative news screening reports, and a complete organizational chart linking all beneficial owners and controllers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border grant disbursements to non-FATF jurisdictions or countries with high money-laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a per-beneficiary due diligence file including sanctioned-entity screening, grant contract or scholarship agreements, justification of charitable objective, monitoring reports, and compliance sign-off by the foundation's AML compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 wire transfers routed through SBP-regulated Panamanian banks via their U.S. correspondent accounts (Fedwire/CHIPS), using payment purpose descriptors such as 'endowment contribution', 'charitable grant', or 'donation for foundation capital'; banks require a written board resolution, donor identification, source-of-funds evidence, and a compliance officer approval before clearing large inbound transfers; no local central bank exchange-control permit is needed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operational and grant payments use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary bank-wire disbursements and SWIFT MT700/MT710 series for commercial documentary letters of credit where the foundation finances trade-linked humanitarian or scientific procurement; clearing occurs through the issuing bank's U.S., U.K., or EU correspondents, with each payment subject to Panama's AML/CFT transaction monitoring thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies
Currency Collar / FX Option Combination (under SBP-permitted derivative clauses)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Filing (Tasa Única Anual) and Corporate Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) via the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 15; staggered schedule based on the company's registration number ending digit (March 1 to March 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a surcharge of up to USD 100 (USD 20 per month of delay); failure to pay for two consecutive years leads to administrative strike-off by the Registro Público and loss of corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (submitted through the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the close of the fiscal year (i.e., by March 31 for calendar-year entities); also required upon any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declaration is subject to fines of up to USD 50,000; persistent failure may result in suspension of corporate rights and administrative penalties against the registered agent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 following the close of the fiscal year (calendar year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties range from USD 30.50 to USD 5,000 depending on duration; overdue taxes accrue monthly interest charges, and continued non-filing can trigger forced collection and tax liens.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Entities with annual gross income exceeding USD 250,000 or total assets exceeding USD 500,000 must undergo an independent statutory audit by a licensed CPA; charitable foundations may apply for an exemption upon DGI approval and submission of alternative financial evidence.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama adopts IFRS for public-interest and listed entities; non-listed entities may use IFRS for SMEs or local fiscal accounting rules (Normas de Información Financiera adoptadas por la DGI).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must confirm the company's ultimate beneficial owners annually within 90 days after each fiscal year-end and upon any share transfer. The confirmation is filed electronically through the registered agent's secure portal; ownership changes must be reflected before March 31 of each year and the UBO register must remain accurate at all times.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Panama CIT flat rate on net Panamanian-source income; 0% effective on exempt private interest foundation income under Law 25 of 1995; territoriality excludes foreign-source income from the tax base)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Private Interest Foundation income exemption under Law 25/1995; charitable non-profit income tax exemption if registered with the DGI; territorial exemption for foreign-source endowment investment income; no capital gains tax on foreign portfolio gains; deductibility of ordinary expenses connected to Panamanian taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 714 (Declaración de Renta para Personas Jurídicas) filed on the DGI electronic portal (Oficina Virtual / SIL) at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 31 March of the year following the fiscal year end; if the fiscal year ends on a date other than 31 December, the return is due within three months after fiscal year end. Nil returns are required for inactive Sociedades Anónimas.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income derived from Panamanian sources, including management fees, local rental income, domestic interest and services performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned S.A. must include only Panama-source income; foreign endowment proceeds, offshore dividends and overseas capital gains are excluded under territoriality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory exemptions, including private interest foundation income, non-profit grants recognized by the DGI, and any legislated tax holiday amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only exemptions supported by a DGI ruling or Law 25/1995 foundation status; attach the foundation certificate and charitable-purpose charter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arithmetic sum of Box 1 and Box 2, representing total gross income reported on the legal entity's books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconciling with the audited financial statement is mandatory; if no Panama activity is conducted, report zero in Box 3 and file a nil return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses wholly incurred for the production of Panamanian taxable income, including local wages, rent, professional services and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign overheads and intra-group charges are deductible only if substantiated, incurred in Panama, and priced at arm's length; keep contracts, invoices and board resolutions available for DGI inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income after deducting Box 4 from Box 1. Losses from Panamanian sources may offset future income for five fiscal years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not offset foreign losses against Panama-source income; if Box 5 is negative, the loss carryforward must be separately tracked in a tax memorandum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed by applying the 25% rate to Box 5, or the non-profit preferential rate when a DGI exemption ruling is valid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-resident shareholder is not taxed on the S.A.'s undistributed profits; the S.A. itself is the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Créditos, retenciones y pagos a cuenta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, withholding tax credits, dividends-advance credits and other recognized prepayments recovered by the entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panamanian withholding credits may be claimed; no credit is granted for foreign taxes paid, in line with territorial income tax principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Impuesto neto a pagar o saldo a favor)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax due after applying Box 7 credits to Box 6; if negative, the result is a refundable or creditable balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid by the statutory deadline; refund requests must be accompanied by supporting certificates and tax residency documents for non-resident claims.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction thereof, capped at 100%; monthly arrears interest at the statutory rate; DGI may issue compulsory collection notices, freeze banking attachments, and criminally prosecute wilful non-filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 716 (Declaración y Pago de Rentas Anticipadas / impuesto adelantado) on the same DGI electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the DGI collection calendar dates for the fiscal period, generally within two months after the end of each calendar quarter (30 June, 30 September, 31 December and 31 March).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual gross Panamanian-source receipts realized during the quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foundation earns no Panamanian income, file the quarterly form as zero or request a formal filing exemption where DGI policy permits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated net taxable income for the quarter using the most recent Form 714 data plus trending adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Estimate must not include foreign-source income; calculations must be consistent with the annual territorial tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative quarterly advance payments already made for the same fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the DGI payment receipts for each quarterly installment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net quarterly instalment due after deducting prior credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made in Panamanian Balboas or US Dollars through an approved banking network; use the entity's registered ''tax ID'' (RUC).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment surcharges apply monthly until regularized; failure to file quarterly advances can invalidate the issuance of a tax solvency certificate (Paz y Salvo) and block public registrations or dividend distributions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividends distributed from Panamanian taxable profits; 0% on dividends originating from foreign-source accumulated profits. An additional 10% corporate-level 'dividend tax' is payable at distribution when exempt profits are distributed without having borne effective corporate income tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority, submit the DGI 'Aplicación de Beneficios de Convenio' request, provide an ownership certificate proving at least the treaty-required participation and holding period, and disclose the ultimate beneficial owner. The reduced withholding rate may be applied at source if the DGI issues prior approval; otherwise, a refund claim for excess tax withheld must be filed within the three-year statute of limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic rates: 12.5% withholding on interest paid to non-residents on financing used in Panama; 20% on royalties for use of intangibles in Panama. Treaty rates generally reduce interest to 5% and royalties to 10% under applicable DTA instruments; a TRC-based application is mandatory to obtain those reductions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. (Balboa) thresholds: Local File required when controlled cross-border transactions exceed B/.1,000,000 in the fiscal year; Master File required when the multinational group has consolidated revenue exceeding B/.50,000,000 and related-party transactions exceed B/.1,000,000. Annual Transfer Pricing Informative Return (Form 792) is due by 30 June of the following fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under Law 254 of 2021 apply to relevant activities including financing, leasing, distribution, shipping and investment management. A charitable endowment manager is subject to ESR if it provides financing or investment management services to related parties. The entity must maintain a registered office in Panama, hold local board meetings, keep minutes of charitable grant decisions, staff appropriately, and retain accounting records at the registered agent. Deficient substance will disqualify tax residency claims, trigger exchange of information, and expose the entity to administrative dissolution risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully filing a false Form 714, omitting Panamanian-source income such as rental income from Panama real estate or interest derived from deposits in a Panamanian bank, or using undisclosed related-party structures to move Panama-source fees to a foreign exempt foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to B/.100,000 and imprisonment from 3 to 5 years; civil fraud penalty of 30% of omitted tax plus arrears interest; DGI may cancel all statutory exemptions and enforce immediate collection through asset attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency, interest and civil penalties; a criminal conviction may trigger travel bans, passport revocation, freezing of personal assets, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Panamanian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a sociedad anónima or private foundation without any real physical office in Panama, without resident management or local decision-making, with no local staff, no board minutes, and with no genuine economic activity; using the entity merely as a letter-box or conduit for charitable donations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2021, fines from B/.1,000 to B/.100,000; cancellation of tax-resident status; removal from the beneficial ownership register; and forced dissolution in cases of complete absence of economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each listed director and the resident agent may be personally fined, barred from incorporating new Panama companies for five years, and ordered to make civil restitution where the shell structure facilitated tax evasion or fraudulent grants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Violations (Law 23 of 2015)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the charitable foundation as a conduit for donations from unidentified sources, disbursing grants to shell entities in high-risk jurisdictions, mixing the settlor's personal assets with charitable funds, and failing to perform customer due diligence on donors and beneficiaries, particularly for wire transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering penalty under the Criminal Code is 5 to 10 years imprisonment for individuals; corporate fines can reach B/.1,000,000; all tainted funds and connected assets are subject to forfeiture; revocation of the foundation's license and inclusion on the national financial intelligence and OFAC sanctions list are automatic outcomes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorize suspicious transfers or who administer the foundation as alter ego of the settlor may be prosecuted personally, subjected to travel bans and extradition, and be required to restore misappropriated charitable assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Tax Evasion and Unlawful Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends without withholding the statutory 10% dividend tax, disguising taxable profits as charitable grants to family members, or paying exorbitant management fees to a non-resident related party without transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monthly surcharge of 5% on the unreported dividend tax up to 100% of the under-withheld amount; disallowance of deductible fees; the company is flagged as a habitual defaulter and blocked from obtaining tax solvency certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who ordered distribution without withholding are civilly liable for the full withholding amount, interest and penalties; where signatures are used to misrepresent a dividend as a grant, directors face criminal fraud or conspiracy charges and a personal travel ban may be imposed.
